about: Dom 2026-10-26 (after /physics1 on his iPhone: five ragdolls + a cut, 0.40 ms a frame): the opponent's body is a physics ragdoll (@frankendom/physics, Jolt WASM, package.json) for PRESENTATION only. The 60 Hz sim (src/fight/duel.ts) and Gate 0 never see it, and nothing it does goes back into the sim. src/fight/ragdoll.ts reads every number and name here. `on`: default on; `?<query>=<v1>` (?physics=v1) = today's death and hit behaviour exactly (the chunk is never fetched). `opponents`: the opponent ids that get a ragdoll, each with the body stem it is drawn in on the 65 rig (src/assets/<body>.glb) and its body measure row per rig (`measure`: rig -> a site path the build copies from the package's data/bodies/, fetched with the chunk; the 106 body, data/rig.json files[body], has its own row from Physics Dev (physics 6ab3c99: minotaur-106.measure.json, 1.7225 m); a rig with no row gets no ragdoll and keeps today's death). `bones`: the package's 20 part ids -> the 65-rig bone names; on a 106 body each goes through data/rig.json `bones` (src/fight/rig-bones.ts bone()), the one 65 -> 106 map, never a second copy. `tickHz` / `maxTicksPerFrame`: the fixed physics step in the scene's own accumulator, beside the sim's. `seed`: the physics world's seed (the engine draws nothing; kept for the package's rand()). `loadAfterFirstFrameMs`: the chunk is imported this long after the first frame, so it never competes with the first visit. `hit`: a landed blow (sim event Hit, the opponent the target) -> the part its location strikes, the impulse (N s) along the attacker's facing plus `lift` up, and the package's stagger (rd.stagger, run on `states.stagger`). `motorTuning`: the package's per-role tracking gain and damping multipliers (keys all < role < part id): 2 / 0.25 for the body (Physics Dev's start), 1 / 1 for the neck and head, which were under-damped at 0.25 on the real clips (#56: settled long-axis median 13.3 deg at 2 / 0.25 vs 3.3 at 1 / 1). `solveHinges`: setTargetPose twists the upper arm / thigh about its long axis so the elbow / knee bend plane matches the clip (physics#14; false = the hinge as built). False here (2026-10-26, measured on the Minotaur's real clips, Mac M5, 15 s of fight each): on, the forearm / hand live median fell 40.7 / 44.0 -> 34.3 / 38.3 deg, but the upper arm rose 24.5 -> 39.2 and its long axis (not just its roll) 15.6 -> 33.5 (settled 6.0 -> 28.1), and the snap at the kill puts that solved upper arm on screen; the arms are not in `hit.blend` either way, so the forearm gain shows nowhere yet. `states`: passed to createPhysics, over the package's data/states.json key by key: `stagger` (Physics Dev's brief: arm 0.9 / forearm 0.6 / hand 0.12, the rest at the torso's 0.6, eased in 0.05 s, held 0.5 s, back over 0.35 s) and `death` (the package's own values: 1 -> 0.01 over 1 s, limp damper 2, sleeps under 0.02 m2/s2 for 4 ticks). `blend`: per part, the share of the ragdoll's pose the bones show at the dip's deepest (the dip's own shape); an unlisted part shows the clip. Only the spine (and half the neck and head) show: measured in the fight (2026-10-26, Mac M5, gain 2 / damping 0.25) the spine tracks the clip within 5 deg median at rest, the arms do not (forearms and hands 40-45 deg median even after a second of settling on one pose: joint limits / hinge axes, not lag), so a share on the arms flings them. `kill`: the killing blow (sim event Killed): the capsules snap onto the killing frame's pose (rd.snapToTarget), then the part by location takes the impulse along the attacker's facing plus `lift`, the death ramp runs and the bones follow the ragdoll until it sleeps; the corpse stays down until the rematch (rd.reset). `blendInS`: seconds from the clip's pose to the ragdoll's after the kill; 0 since the snap (no pop measured at 0/2/4 ticks). `finisher`: what a ragdolled opponent's kill does with the finisher rotation, `default` unless `?<query>=<a key of values>`. `keep` (default): a cinematic finisher (Split Crown, Decapitation, Run Through, Opened) plays exactly as before and gets no ragdoll; only the plain death (the rotation's no-ceremony outcome, about 1 blade kill in 5, and every kick and skill kill) falls as a ragdoll. `skip` (?ragdoll=always, Dom's phone test 2026-10-26): every death of his is the plain death and falls as a ragdoll; the finisher (picture and its death cue) is skipped for that kill.
